On-site audio: evidence status (2,983 clips total)

A clip with a structural description has at least one documented musical feature. This does not mean that every feature in the recording has been verified.

Understanding entry types and evidence

Evidence is recorded separately for each feature. For example, a drum clip may have a 6/8 time signature supplied by its source, while its kick placement was checked against MIDI note onsets. A named pattern does not imply that the performance or work is famous. A short clip may not contain the full structure shown in a performance chart. Structural descriptions do not mean that every recording has been independently assessed by ear. Unclassified means that no classification has been assigned under the current criteria, not that the music has no relevant features.

English descriptions preserve the source records’ qualifications and verification status. Japanese work titles are romanized; original names remain searchable.
